question.text: Let $a_n$ denote the term independent of $x$ in the expansion of $\left[x+\frac{\sin (1 / n)}{x^2}\right]^{3 n}$, then $\lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{\left(a_n\right) n!}{{ }^{3 n} P_n}$ equals

solution.text:
$\left[x+\frac{\sin (1 / n)}{x^2}\right]^{3 n}$
$\begin{aligned}
& T_{r+1}={ }^{3 n} C_r(x)^{3 n-r}\left(\frac{\sin (1 / n)}{x^2}\right)^r \\
& ={ }^{3 n} C_r(x)^{3 n-3 r}(\sin (1 / n))^r \\
& r=n
\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}
& a_n={ }^{3 n} C_n(\sin (1 / n))^n \\
& \lim _{n \rightarrow \infty} \frac{{ }^{3 n} C_n(\sin (1 / n))^n \cdot n!}{{ }^{3 n} P_n}=0
\end{aligned}$
